page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture with 24 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 2880 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several areas. Single-core execution is highly efficient, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3702.98 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2771.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also in the top 10%, with large-block read-only speeds at 414.9 GB/sec and write speeds at 213.09 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 26345.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 82776.54. The system supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, which aids in high-throughput tasks like bzip3 decompression and static web serving.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated 2880 GB NVMe SSD provide a dense resource profile that minimizes the need for external storage attachments. However, a potential tradeoff is the 2.0 GHz base clock speed, which, while highly capable in parallel execution, may limit workloads requiring extreme single-thread clock frequencies. The instance is highly suited for memory-intensive and database workloads, including large-scale Redis deployments, relational databases, data compilation, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
